chunks.text: A guarantee exceeding twelve months or the branch authorisation limit requires escalation to the next approval level; the amount and tenor must come from confirmed fields, not model guesses.

Transactions involving sanctioned countries, regions or parties must first complete formal sanctions screening. A company name in the document does not prove screening has passed; the assistant can only prompt verification.

Guarantee versions, approval opinions and audit events are retained under the approved retention policy; ordinary logs must not record full customer text, identity data or hidden model chain-of-thought.

Over-limit business is escalated by amount and risk: branch, regional approval centre, head office. Escalation opinions and approval evidence must be recorded in the approval workflow and cannot be backfilled later.

Origination, review, disbursement and accounting roles must be separated; the same person must not complete customer onboarding and guarantee issuance review together. Exceptions require compliance approval and an audit trail.

If sanctions screening hits or information is insufficient, the business unit must not release the transaction on its own; it must escalate to compliance and follow the sanctions policy. Conclusions and evidence must be archived.

chunks.title_path: Internal policy / Operational risk / Incident reporting
chunks.text: Operational errors, over-authorised approvals or customer complaints must be reported to operational risk on the same day, retaining the incident record, impact scope and remediation evidence.
Outsourcing or third-party services require due diligence, a data-security assessment and contract approval; customer data must not be provided to unapproved third parties.
